Predicted probabilities of a fitted multispecies model

Source: R/fp_occu_ms-outputs.R
predict.fp_occu_ms.Rd

The occupancy probability or the false-positive rate of each species of an fp_occu_ms() fit, from the coefficients of that species, as predict.fp_occu() gives them for one species. Random effects on the false-positive rate (fp_group, random_fp) are left out, as in predict.fp_occu(). In development, as fp_occu_ms().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  process = c("occ", "fp"),
  species = NULL,
  prob = 0.95,
  summary = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An fp_occu_ms object.

newdata

Data frame with the covariates of the requested process. Without a column of species (the species column of the data), every row is predicted for every species in species; with it, each row for its own species. If missing, the sites used in the fit, for every species; for a false-positive rate with covariates measured on each occasion, the automated occasions of each species, with the covariates of their sites.

process

"occ" for the occupancy probability or "fp" for the false-positive rate, both at the site level.

species

Names of the species to predict when newdata has no column of species. The default, NULL, is every species.

prob

Width of the equal-tailed credible interval.

summary

Logical. Return a summary per row (TRUE) or the matrix of posterior draws (rows are draws, columns are rows of newdata)?

...

Unused, or passed on (see each method).

Value

A data frame with the rows of newdata (repeated for each species when it has no column of species), the species column, and the posterior mean and credible interval of the probability; or, with summary = FALSE, the matrix of draws, with rows as draws and columns as the rows of that data frame.

See also

fp_occu_ms(), predict.fp_occu()

Examples

# \donttest{
s <- simulate_fp_ms(nspecies = 4, nsite = 60, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu_ms(s$data, occ = ~ x, det = ~ bio, random_recorder = FALSE,
                chains = 2, threads_per_chain = 1)
#> Parametrization (4 species at 60 sites): centered = FALSE, centered_occ = FALSE; see ?fp_occu_ms.
#> Running MCMC with 2 parallel chains, with 1 thread(s) per chain...
#> 
#> Chain 1 finished in 99.6 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 107.6 seconds.
#> 
#> Both chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 103.6 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 107.7 seconds.
#> 
#> Warning: Largest R-hat is 1.013 (> 1.01); run longer chains.
predict(m, newdata = data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1)))
#>     x species  estimate     lower     upper

#> 2   0     sp1 0.6047237 0.4508931 0.7697389

#> 6   1     sp2 0.4789149 0.3065087 0.6602128
#> 7  -1     sp3 0.4504723 0.2919431 0.5988758
#> 8   0     sp3 0.4330593 0.3086327 0.5486169
#> 9   1     sp3 0.4174396 0.2597201 0.5787053
